messages:
maya: Quick sync — our loadtest numbers for the llama-13b config are ~18% worse on staging vs dev even though the model + prompt set and traffic shape are identical. I dug into a few traces and I think environment parity is the main culprit (drivers/container/kernel flags) + KV cache warmup mismatch.

ana: Ugh. That lines up with what I saw last week — different CUDA driver microversions pick different GEMM kernels. Do we have exact image digests pinned for both clusters?

maya: Not everywhere. Dev uses redwood/runtime:v3.2-cuda12.1@sha256:abcd1234, staging is using v3.2-cuda12.1 (floating tag). Also dev nodes are 525.85.12 driver, staging is 525.105.17.

kevin: Floating tags + driver diff = guaranteed kernel selection drift. nvprof/cupti traces will show which kernels were chosen. I saw cuBLASLt vs cutlass_wmma variants switch with 525.10x.

josh: Do we know if kernel selection is also influenced by env flags? e.g. REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL or TF32 settings?

maya: Yes — runtime honors env vars: REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL (cutlass|cublas|auto) and RUNTIME_TF32_OVERRIDE. Staging had REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL unset; dev had REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=cutlass (entered by a debug script).

ana: That could explain throughput. Also KV cache coverage was different: dev warmup workload prefilled prefixes with ~1.2M keys before test, staging only did a cold start. Synthetic load tests often miss realistic KV hit rates.

kevin: Agenda: (1) define apples-to-apples parity checklist, (2) add replay harness options to enforce KV warm and sequence-length distribution, (3) pin image and driver versions for calibration runs.

maya: Proposed parity checklist (short):
- exact container image digest (no floating tags)
- same NVIDIA driver microversion (e.g., 525.85.12)
- matching CUDA toolkit inside image (12.1)
- identical REDWOOD_* env vars and kernel-forcing flags
- same kernel/GPU power governor and CPU frequency scaling settings
- same container runtime flags (e.g., --shm-size, --ulimit memlock)
- KV cache warmup step (explicit count)

josh: I can add CLI flags to the replay harness: --kv-warmup-count, --seq-dist-file, --preserve-timing to mimic interarrival. That should make synthetic closer to recorded traffic.

ci-bot: Deploy check: staging fleet images do not match digest abcd1234. See CI job #5423. :eyes:

ana: For profiling, recommend capturing these three artifacts per run: nvprof/cupti timeline, runtime kernel-selection log (runtime emits kernel candidates + scores), and perf counters (SM utilization + l2 hit rate).

kevin: Quick snippet for an apples-to-apples run in staging (example):
```bash
# pin image + driver on nodepool
kubectl set image ds/runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:v3.2-cuda12.1@sha256:abcd1234 -n redwood
# set env to force same kernels
kubectl set env ds/runtime REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=cutlass RUNTIME_TF32_OVERRIDE=1 -n redwood
# run replay with kv warmup
rwd-replay run --trace traces/2026-03-10.trace --kv-warmup-count 1200000 --preserve-timing --seq-dist-file seqdist.json --out result.json
```

josh: Also add a small warmup phase before measurement window in loadtest driver: 30s KV-only warmups + 120s mixed traffic. Otherwise p50/p95 are noisy.

maya: FYI profiling from the two runs I pulled:
- dev (cutlass forced): tokens/sec = 9.8k, average SM util 92%, top kernels: cutlass_wmma_gemm, kv_lookup_kernel_fast
- staging (default): tokens/sec = 8.3k, average SM util 68%, top kernels: cublasLtGemmAlgo1, kv_lookup_kernel_slow
So staging picked a cublasLt path and our KV lookup had significantly higher L2 miss rate.

kevin: Interesting — KV lookup slow path likely due to allocator differences (glibc malloc arenas, jemalloc vs tcmalloc) and CPU pinning. Check MALLOC_ARENA_MAX and LD_PRELOAD around.

ana: I'll add a small test matrix: vary driver microversion (525.85.12 vs 525.105.17) x container digest pinned vs floating x REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL set vs unset. Run each cell with the exact same replay trace and kv-warmup.

maya: One more gotcha — tensor layout alignment changed by our build when compiled with a different host glibc header. Need to pin the runtime base image digest too.

josh: Action items:
- ana: create the parity checklist PR and add to runbook (low effort).
- kevin: prepare tracing template + perf-counter dashboard.
- josh: add replay harness flags and KV warm metrics.
- maya: orchestrate 3x calibration runs on staging pinned to dev image/driver and share artifacts.

deploy-bot: Scheduled calibration run triggered: cal-1760004321 — status: queued.

maya: Thanks — aim to have first calibration results by EOD tomorrow. If we can enforce full parity we should see the kernel selection converge and the numbers line up. :white_check_mark:
